title: BMW Motor Sports — Oct 2, 2026
html:
IMSA

  • No IMSA race in the last 7 days — Last round was the TireRack.com Battle on the Bricks at Indianapolis (Sep 20), won by BMW M Team WRT. source
  • Next: Motul Petit Le Mans, Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta — Event Sep 30 – Oct 3, 2026; 10-hour season finale Saturday, Oct 3, 12:10 PM – 10:10 PM ET. source
  • Practice 2 (Oct 1) — #24 BMW M Hybrid V8 (BMW M Team WRT; Sheldon van der Linde / Dries Vanthoor / Robin Frijns, GTP) 3rd fastest, 1:10.727, 0.088s off P1; #25 BMW M Hybrid V8 4th. #48 Paul Miller Racing BMW M4 GT3 EVO also entered (GTD). source

WEC

  • 6 Hours of Fuji, Fuji Speedway — Sep 27, 2026 (LMGT3) — #32 Team WRT BMW M4 GT3 EVO (Augusto Farfus / Sean Gelael / Darren Leung) WON the class; #69 Team WRT BMW M4 GT3 EVO 6th in class. source
  • 6 Hours of Fuji (Hypercar) — #15 BMW M Team WRT M Hybrid V8 (Kevin Magnussen / Raffaele Marciello / Dries Vanthoor) 3rd — ran 2nd on used tyres until passed by Alpine late; #20 BMW M Team WRT (Robin Frijns / René Rast / Sheldon van der Linde) 13th, 1 lap down. Winner: #8 Toyota. source
  • Next round: 6 Hours of Barcelona — Oct 17–18, 2026 (race Oct 18) — just outside the 14-day window. source

DTM / BMW M2 Cup

  • No races this week; next round: DTM Hockenheim Finale + BMW M2 Cup, Hockenheimring — Oct 10–11, 2026 (per BMW M racing calendar). Schubert Motorsport runs two BMW M4 GT3 EVOs (Marco Wittmann, Kelvin van der Linde); Wittmann went into the finale 3rd in points, 24 behind the leader after his Sachsenring win (Sep 12). source

WorldSBK

  • Cremona, Italy — Sep 26–27, 2026 (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team, BMW M 1000 RR) — Danilo Petrucci: 14th Race 1, 11th Superpole Race, 12th Race 2 (Superpole 19th). Miguel Oliveira: crashed out of Race 2 while running as high as 5th; per BMW, also DNF Race 1 and 8th in Superpole Race. Nicolò Bulega (Ducati) clinched the 2026 title. source
  • Next: Estoril, Portugal — Oct 9–11, 2026; season finale at Jerez Oct 16–18. source

FIM EWC

  • Season complete — no races this week — BMW Motorrad World Endurance Team #37 (Michael van der Mark / Markus Reiterberger / Steven Odendaal) won the Bol d'Or finale at Le Castellet (Sep 17–20) from pole and clinched the 2026 FIM EWC title, 158–154 over YART — first EWC title for a European manufacturer. source

Technical & Driver News

No driver lineup changes or new technical announcements found in the last 7 days.

  • M4 GT3 EVO: Shanghai 8 Hours win (Sep 25–27) — #18 Team KRC (Max Hesse / Zhang Mingyang / Zhang Zhendong) won by ~1:30; also Barber GTWC America: #29 Turner (Foley / Rothberg) 4th Pro. source
  • Upcoming: Indianapolis 8 Hour (Oct 8–10) — IGTC / GTWC America finale with three M4 GT3 EVOs; #29 Turner (Foley / Rothberg / Connor De Phillippi) — Foley & Rothberg in Pro title contention. source

Coverage gaps: dtm.com pages need JavaScript and could not be read (Hockenheim date from BMW M calendar; no DTM/M2 Cup results check); worldsbk.com Cremona results PDF and main race report not reachable (401) — Oliveira Race 1 / Superpole Race results from BMW press only; fimewc.com pages returned 403 (EWC confirmed via BMW press); IMSA entry-list PDF not checked; #69 WEC LMGT3 driver names not verified.

title: Weekly Wine Report — Oct 2, 2026
html:
What's Popular Now

  • Aubert dominates California Pinot — Wine Spectator's California Pinot Noir report (Sep 30, 750+ wines) is topped by Aubert, with two Sonoma Coast bottlings at 96–97 points. source
  • Boisset buys Artesa (Carneros) — Jean-Charles Boisset acquired Artesa's brand and 350-acre estate from Raventós Codorníu (Sep 23); price undisclosed. Decanter also covered it Sep 24. source
  • U.S. ban on Canadian alcoholic beverages takes effect — Trade-war escalation cutting off Canadian wine imports (Wine Spectator, Sep 29). source
  • Value: Banshee Pinot Noir Sonoma County 2023 — 90 pts Wine Spectator, $30. Also Architect Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast 2024 — 89 pts WS, $25. source
  • Splurge: Aubert Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast CIX 2024 — 97 pts Wine Spectator, $125. Also Domaine de la Côte Pinot Noir Sta. Rita Hills La Côte 2024 — 96 pts WS, $399/1.5L. source

Pinot Noir

  • Aubert Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast CIX 2024 — 97 pts Wine Spectator (James Molesworth), $125; top wine of the Sep 30 California Pinot Noir report. source
  • Aubert Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast UV Vineyard 2024 — 96 pts Wine Spectator, $105. source
  • Brewer-Clifton Pinot Noir Sta. Rita Hills Machado 2024 — 96 pts Wine Spectator, $85. source
  • Calera Pinot Noir Mount Harlan de Villiers Vineyard 2023 — 96 pts Wine Spectator, $100. source
  • Broadbent Pinot Noir Central Coast 2024 — 87 pts Wine Spectator, $15 (budget pick). source

Napa Cabernet Sauvignon

  • No new Napa Cab scores verified this window — Wine Spectator's California Cabernet issue is dated Nov 15; recent Cab reviews seen were older or paywalled. source
  • Napa news: Boisset acquires Artesa — 150 planted acres across Carneros and Mt. Veeder; plans organic/biodynamic conversion; winemaker Paula Borgo stays (Sep 23). source
  • Napa news: Honig lists ingredients on labels — First Napa winery to do so, starting with its 2025 Sauvignon Blanc Napa Valley (Wine Spectator, Oct 2). source
  • Wine Star Award nominees — Napa's Pine Ridge Vineyards and Grgich Hills Estate are nominated for Wine Enthusiast's American Winery of the Year (updated Sep 22). source

Paso Robles

  • Saxum's new coastal vineyard — Justin Smith is planting Syrah at Cayucos Ridge, a 1,600-ft Santa Lucia ridgeline under 4 miles from the ocean, west of Paso (Wine Spectator, Sep 17; just outside the 14-day window). No wine scores disclosed. source

Vinous Napa/Paso reviews and several Wine Spectator Napa Cab and California Rhône articles paywalled — scores omitted. Wine Spectator Oct 31 Advance page returned an error. MAHA Estate (Paso) 95-pt Understory 2023 article was undated, so left out.
